title: Degradation controlplane patterns
summary: Working notes for a compact, operator-friendly control-plane approach that enforces deterministic graceful degradation across model variants, tenant slices, and regions. Focus on auditable decisioning and measurable user impact
background: We operate heterogeneous fleets (hosted + dedicated + private). When pressure or failures happen we tend to have ad-hoc fallbacks. Need a small set of patterns that control-plane teams can reuse, with clear telemetry requirements and safe rollout steps.
objectives: Create a small vocabulary for degradation levels (L0..L3) and map model builds to them
Specify capacity-slicing semantics for multi-tenant pools and how admission control interacts with downgrade
Define control-plane policy primitives and examples operators can apply
List concrete testing/rollout steps and telemetry to validate user impact
Document operational runbook actions tied to each degradation trigger
architecture-overview: Pattern: treat each request as (tenant, route, region, cost_estimate). Control plane evaluates policy predicates and yields an ordered candidate list of (variant, capacity_slice, region_target). Runtime enforces deterministic step-down and reports chosen_variant and reason. Cross-region spillover is conditional on route-level latency budget and region health signals.
capacity-slicing-rules: Named slices: premium, standard, best-effort; slices carry soft token/sec and concurrency targets
Steady-state reservation for premium slice; standard can burst into reserved free capacity; best-effort is lowest priority
Admission procedure: pre-check token-budget -> if exceed then attempt bounded queue -> if queue full then degrade model -> if degrade impossible then reject
Slice quotas are per-tenant per-region. Cross-region pooling only used for spillover after local downgrade fails within latency budget
graceful-degradation-ladder: L0 - Full fidelity: float/FP16 or high-precision quantized model, full KV caching, full context window
L1 - Performance-optimized: aggressive quantization (e.g., 8-bit), fewer decoding passes, warmed caches where possible
L2 - Distilled/medium: smaller architecture with similar API but reduced reasoning fidelity and shorter context support
L3 - Best-effort tiny: minimal model for syntactic/completion tasks; last-resort fallback or short-answer-only mode
policy-primitives-examples: match(T): boolean predicate on request metadata (tenant, route, prompt_length)
prefer: ordered list of variants annotated with degradation level and latency/cost guards
latency_budget_ms: numeric guard used for cross-region decisions
spillover: allow|deny with ordered region preference

Example policy (stringified): "policy finance-payments { match: tenant ==\"enterprise\" && route == \"document-summarize\"; prefer: [\"llm-xl-v3@L0\", \"llm-xl-v3-8bit@L1\"]; fallback: [\"llm-m-distilled@L2\"]; latency_budget_ms: 320; spillover: allow(region_order=[\"us-west-2\",\"us-east-1\"]); }"
runtime-behaviors: Deterministic step-down: runtime must try variants in declared order; never randomly sample competing variants during pressure
Guarded spillover: do cross-region routing only if estimated RTT + processing <= latency_budget_ms
Quota-first: when slice quota exceeded, prefer bounded queueing before model downgrade for short spikes
Context-aware selection: for long prompts prefer variants that support larger context even if higher cost; policy can declare route_hint=long_context
telemetry-and-alerting: Per-policy metrics: chosen_variant, fallback_count, queue_drops, reject_count
Quality hooks: golden-prompt scoring for L0 vs L1/L2 cohorts and drift alerts if score delta > threshold
Operational alerts: sustained fallback_rate > 5% over 10m -> ops; cross-region-spillover > 15% traffic -> paging
Cost telemetry: token_cost_estimate per-request and rolling tenant spend delta when policies change
testing-and-rollout: Shadow mode: evaluate policy decisions and log differences without altering live routing for 24-72h
Canary: route subset (1-5%) through new policy with automated quality comparison on golden prompts
Chaos test: simulated region blackhole + load spike to validate deterministic step-down and runbook triggers
Preflight checks: policy vetter rejects policies that raise expected avg token cost for premium tenants without approval
operational-runbook: Variant unhealthy: control plane flags variant -> runtime steps to next ladder level; operator investigates GPU errors, kernel logs, infra metrics
Unplanned cross-region spillover: confirm latency budgets, check region health, redeploy compatible model builds to target region or enable burst pools
High fallback rate alert: investigate root cause (scaling misconfig, model regression, traffic pattern change); rollback policy pointer if needed
Emergency rollback: immediate policy pointer swap to last stable version triggers deterministic mapping and restores previous behavior
open-questions: Expose degradation info to customers (response header) vs keep internal-only? Tradeoffs include transparency vs surface area for abuse
How to maintain tokenizer and behavior compatibility across quantized/distilled builds? Need automated semantic regression tests
Should we support fractional degradation (e.g., A/B across variants) or stick to deterministic ladders for predictability?
What SLA commitments can we promise for Dedicated vs Hosted when degradation occurs? Need legal/product alignment
